name: Dinutuximab + GM-CSF + IL-2 + Isotretinoin (High-Risk Neuroblastoma Maintenance)

source.textbook: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.

institution.provenance: ONCQIS Landmark Regimen: COG ANBL0032 Phase III Trial (Yu et al. NEJM 2010)

premedications.name: Hydromorphone or Morphine continuous IV
premedications.notes: Mandatory: begin continuous opioid infusion 1-2 hours prior to dinutuximab and continue for 2 hours post-infusion to control severe neuropathic pain.

supportiveCare: Mandatory intensive pain management: GD2 targeting causes intense allodynia and neuropathic pain.
Capillary leak syndrome monitoring: monitor daily weights, edema, albumin, and blood pressure.
monitoring: Vitals q15m during first hour of dinutuximab infusion, then q30m-1h
Daily CBC, CMP, urinalysis during inpatient administration
Neurological assessment for transverse myelitis, peripheral neuropathy, and visual acuity

doseModificationRules.condition: Severe neuropathic pain unresponsive to maximum opioid escalation
doseModificationRules.text: Reduce infusion rate by 50% or pause dinutuximab infusion. Re-titrate opioid analgesia. Resume at slower rate once pain is controlled.
Discontinue dinutuximab and IL-2 immediately. Provide respiratory support and careful fluid resuscitation with albumin.

drugs.name: Dinutuximab
drugs.notes: Dinutuximab 17.5 mg/m2/day continuous IV infusion over 10-20 hours on Days 4-7 of each 28-day cycle (total 70 mg/m2/cycle) with GM-CSF (Cycles 1, 3, 5) or IL-2 (Cycles 2, 4) plus isotretinoin. Grounded in COG ANBL0032 trial.
